name: Italian Poker
description: Poker all'italiana is a draw poker variant played with a short deck (32, 36 or 40 cards by player count). It has optional blind opening (buio), two betting rounds with a draw in between, and a non-standard hand ranking where flush beats full house and straight flushes have min-medium-max tie rules.
deck: Short deck: 32 cards (7 to Ace) for 4 players, 36 (6 to Ace) for 5, 40 (5 to Ace) for 6, from a standard 52-card pack.

setup.deck: Short deck of 32 (4 players), 36 (5) or 40 (6) cards from a standard 52-card pack; lowest rank is 11 minus number of players.
setup.dealing: All players ante (invito). Optionally the first player may open blind (buio) before the deal; then dealer gives 5 cards each, one at a time clockwise starting to dealer's left.
setup.equipment: Standard deck (short pack), chips for betting; ante amount and min/max limits agreed before play.

rules.objective: Win the pot by having the highest-ranking hand at showdown, or by being the last player standing when all others have folded.
rules.gameplay: Ante; optional blind (buio, controbuio, over) before deal. Deal 5 cards each. First betting round: pass or open (with pair of Jacks or better, or 4-card straight-flush draw); then fold, call, raise. Draw: each surviving player may exchange 0–4 cards. Second betting round: bet, check, or parol (throw in and carry pot); then fold, call, raise. Showdown: highest hand wins; flush beats full house; straight flush has min/medium/max with min beating max.
keyRules: Opening requires pair of Jacks or better, or four consecutive cards of a suit (no Ace) that can extend to straight flush.
Flush ranks above full house. Straight flush: minimum beats maximum, maximum beats medium, medium beats minimum.
Ties broken by suit order: hearts highest, then diamonds, clubs, spades.
